prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1071; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Insured reports vehicles made contact at low speed in the eastbound lane. Insured states no airbag deployment and both vehicles were driven from the scene. Claimant reports neck and back strain and has retained counsel. Counsel has requested that all communication be directed to their office. Initial file set up and liability investigation assigned.

Entry 2: Police report obtained and reviewed. Report documents the other driver as at fault for crossing the centerline. Photos of both vehicles received from the insured show minor front-end damage with no structural deformation noted. Independent appraisal requested. Counsel's office acknowledged receipt of the notice of representation and confirmed they will send medical records once available.

Entry 3: Recorded statement taken from the insured, consistent with the initial report. Insured confirms seatbelt was worn and no distraction was involved. Appraiser estimate received and reviewed. Repair scope approved pending a supplement check for hidden damage. Medical authorization forms requested through counsel. No response received yet.

Entry 4: Claimant's counsel forwarded initial treatment records indicating diagnosis of cervical and lumbar strain. Records show physical therapy referral and a follow-up scheduled in several weeks. Medical review assigned to evaluate whether treatment is consistent with the reported mechanism of impact. Reserve adjusted to reflect the current injury and treatment plan.

Entry 5: Medical review completed with notes that the reported soft tissue injuries are consistent with a low-speed impact. Requested itemized treatment bills and wage documentation from counsel. Counsel indicated a settlement demand will follow after treatment concludes. File diary set for follow-up. Claim remains open pending receipt of outstanding documents.
